messages:
maria (TenantCorp): Hey team, one of our engineers lost edit rights on a project in the console. Was project-admin yesterday, now when they open Project Settings they get a 403.

alex.support: sorry to hear that. Can you confirm the user id and exact time you saw the 403? Screenshot helps too.

maria (TenantCorp): user U-79234, happened at 2024-10-12T18:12:03Z. Screenshot: https://tenantcorp.screens/403-project-edit.png

alex.support: thx. Do you see any network error for the request to /v1/console/projects/:id/permissions? If so paste the response body (redact PII).

maria (TenantCorp): response: `{ "error": "forbidden", "reason": "missing_scope", "required": "projects:edit" }`

alex.support: that indicates the access token used for the console request doesn't have the projects:edit scope. Did you change SSO or tokens recently?

maria (TenantCorp): we rotated our on-prem auth proxy last week. No other changes AFAIK.

sam.eng-sre: jumping in. Could be our proxy doing a token exchange and dropping the scp claim. Can you DM the raw bearer token to @alex.support so we can decode? If not, paste the JWT claims (redacted).

maria (TenantCorp): DM sent.

alex.support: decoded claims (redacted): `iss: https://idp.tenantcorp, sub: U-79234, aud: ["redwood-inference"], exp: 1700000000, iat: 1699996400, scope: "projects:view embeddings:read"`

sam.eng-sre: aha scope claim shows projects:view only. Our console needs projects:edit for the settings call. Was the token issued directly by IdP or minted by your proxy?

maria (TenantCorp): proxy exchanges the upstream SAML assertion for a short-lived bearer that the console uses. The IdP still returns full scopes when we test directly.

jen.eng-iam: quick note — we added a conservative scope mapping for delegated tokens in the proxy last month to avoid over-privileged exchanges. Wondering if the proxy mapping defaults to view-only for console flows.

deploy-bot: config-change: auth-proxy-v2 deployed to tenantcorp-prod at 2024-10-05T03:22:11Z (sha: a1b2c3).

sam.eng-sre: that matches timing. Maria, can you ask your proxy team to check the token-exchange mapping for the audience and scp claims? Common issues: 1) mapping only includes `scp` entries that match a whitelist, 2) audience rewriting removes a model-service audience which triggers a scope prune, 3) header size overflow truncates claims.

maria (TenantCorp): I'm on it. I asked our infra lead to dump the proxy token mapping logs and they found a rule that strips unknown scopes. Looks like `projects:edit` wasn't in the whitelist.

alex.support: ok so root cause = proxy RBAC scope pruning. Two recommended fixes: 1) add projects:edit to proxy allowed scopes for console exchange, 2) change proxy to forward raw idp `scp` claim (if policy allows) or perform a proper token exchange via our recommended OIDC flow.

jen.eng-iam: we'll also add a safety check on our side: if a console permissions call returns missing_scope, the Console UI will show a clearer message instructing admins to check delegated token scope mapping (ticket: ENG-IAM-4723).

maria (TenantCorp): quick fix applied on our side: whitelist updated and tokens re-issued. Confirmed editor can now open Project Settings and edit. Thanks!

alex.support: great. Closing loop: please keep the deployed proxy change id and timeline in case of audit. Also if you can share the proxy rule snippet (redacted) that would help us add guidance to our docs.

maria (TenantCorp): will share redacted rule in #vendor-auth later today.

sam.eng-sre: internal follow-up: add a diagnostic to the console that fetches token claims when a 403 occurs (opt-in, logs only) so we can surface missing scopes automatically. Filing ENG-SRE-1998.

deploy-bot: incident-note: no platform outage. Customer-level config issue.

alex.support: glad it's resolved. Closing thread — reopen if it reoccurs. :thumbsup:
